items.title: What the Dying Mind Perceives: From Light to Dark, or Dark to Light

items.zh: 若俱平等曾串習者，彼於爾時，隨初自憶，或他令憶，唯此不捨，不起餘心。彼於爾時，由二種因增上力故，而便命終。謂樂著戲論因增上力，及淨不淨業因增上力。
items.en: If one's wholesome and unwholesome habituation has been roughly equal, then at that time, whichever comes to mind first — recalled by oneself or by another — is held to alone, and no other thought arises. At that time, death comes about through the dominant force of two causes: the dominant force of delight in elaboration, and the dominant force of pure and impure karma.

items.zh: 受盡先業所引果已，若行不善業者，當於爾時，受先所作諸不善業所得不愛果之前相，猶如夢中見無量種變怪色相。依此相故，薄伽梵說：若有先作惡不善業及增長已，彼於爾時，如日後分，或山山峯影等懸覆、遍覆、極覆。當知如是補特伽羅從明趣闇。
items.en: Once the result brought about by one's past karma has been fully spent, if one has practised unwholesome deeds, then at that time one experiences the foretoken of the undesirable result those deeds will bring — as if seeing, in a dream, countless strange and startling forms. On account of this sign, the Blessed One said: if one has committed unwholesome deeds and let them grow, then at that time it is like the late afternoon sun overshadowed by mountain peaks — first partly overshadowed, then wholly overshadowed, then utterly overshadowed. Such a person should be understood as going from light into darkness.

items.zh: 若先受盡不善業果而修善者，與上相違。當知如是補特伽羅從闇趣明。此中差別者，將命終時，猶如夢中見無量種非變怪色可意相生。
items.en: If one has already fully spent the results of unwholesome deeds and has since practised what is wholesome, the opposite occurs: such a person should be understood as going from darkness into light. The distinguishing mark is that, as death approaches, one sees, as in a dream, countless agreeable forms — not strange or startling ones.

items.zh: 若作上品不善業者，彼由見斯變怪相故，流汗毛竪，手足紛亂，遂失便穢，捫摸虛空，翻睛咀沫。彼於爾時，有如是等變怪相生。若造中品不善業者，彼於爾時，變怪之相或有或無，設有不具。
items.en: One who has done unwholesome deeds of the highest degree, because they see these disturbing signs, sweats, their hair stands on end, their hands and feet thrash about, they lose control of their bowels, grope at the empty air, roll their eyes, and froth at the mouth. At that time, disturbing signs such as these arise. For one who has done unwholesome deeds of the middle degree, at that time the disturbing signs may or may not appear, and if they do, not all of them.

items.title: Self-Love and the Arising of the Intermediate State

items.zh: 又諸眾生將命終時，乃至未到惛昧想位，長時所習我愛現行。由此力故，謂我當無，便愛自身。由此建立中有、生報。
items.en: Further, as beings are about to die, right up until they reach the state of dim, indistinct thought, the long-habituated self-love becomes active. Through the force of this, thinking "I am about to cease to be," one comes to love one's own self all the more. Through this, the intermediate state and the resulting rebirth are established.

items.zh: 若預流果及一來果，爾時我愛亦復現行。然此預流及一來果，於此我愛，由智慧力數數推求，制而不著。猶壯丈夫與羸劣者共相捔力，能制伏之。當知此中道理亦爾。若不還果，爾時我愛不復現行。
items.en: For a stream-enterer or a once-returner, self-love likewise becomes active at that time. Yet these noble ones, through the power of wisdom, examine this self-love again and again, restraining it so as not to become attached — as a strong man wrestling a weak one easily overpowers him; the principle here should be understood the same way. For a non-returner, self-love no longer becomes active at that time at all.

items.zh: 又解肢節，除天、那落迦，所餘生處一切皆有。此復二種。一、重，二、輕。重謂作惡業者，輕謂作善業者。北拘盧洲一切皆輕。又色界沒時，皆具諸根。欲界沒時、隨所有根，或具、不具。又清淨解脫死者，名調善死。不清淨不解脫死者，名不調善死。
items.en: Further, the loosening of the limbs [at death] occurs in every realm of rebirth except among the gods and in the hells; this is again of two kinds — severe and mild. It is severe for one who has done unwholesome deeds, and mild for one who has done wholesome deeds; in the Northern Continent it is always mild. Further, when beings of the form realm pass away, their faculties are always whole; when beings of the desire realm pass away, their faculties may be whole or not. Further, one who dies pure and liberated is said to die "composed"; one who dies impure and unliberated is said to die "uncomposed."

items.zh: 又將終時，作惡業者，識於所依從上分捨。即從上分冷觸隨起，如此漸捨乃至心處。造善業者，識於所依從下分捨。即從下分冷觸隨起，如此漸捨乃至心處。當知後識唯心處捨。從此冷觸遍滿所依。
items.en: Further, as death approaches, for one who has done unwholesome deeds, consciousness withdraws from its bodily support beginning from the upper part; a sensation of cold follows from the upper part, and it withdraws in this way, gradually, down to the region of the heart. For one who has done wholesome deeds, consciousness withdraws beginning from the lower part; a sensation of cold follows from the lower part, and it withdraws in this way, gradually, up to the region of the heart. It should be understood that consciousness withdraws last only from the region of the heart, after which the sensation of cold spreads through the whole of its bodily support.

items.zh: 云何生？由我愛無間已生故，無始樂著戲論因已熏習故，淨不淨業因已熏習故。彼所依體由二種因增上力故，從自種子，即於是處中有、異熟無間得生。死生同時，如秤兩頭，低昂時等。
items.en: What is birth? Because self-love has arisen without interruption; because the cause of delight in elaboration has been perfumed [into seed] since beginningless time; and because the cause of pure and impure karma has been perfumed [into seed] — through the dominant force of these two causes, the being's underlying continuum, from its own seeds, gives rise without interruption, in the appropriate place, to the intermediate being and then to the ripened result. Death and birth are simultaneous, like the two ends of a scale: as one end sinks, the other rises, at one and the same time.

items.zh: 而此中有必具諸根。造惡業者所得中有，如黑羺光、或陰闇夜。作善業者所得中有，如白衣光、或晴明夜。又此中有是極清淨天眼所行。
items.en: This intermediate being always has all its faculties complete. The intermediate being obtained by one who has done unwholesome deeds is like the dim light off a black sheep, or like a dark, overcast night. The intermediate being obtained by one who has done wholesome deeds is like the light off white cloth, or like a clear, moonlit night. This intermediate being can only be perceived by the most purified divine sight.

items.zh: 彼於爾時，先我愛類不復現行，識已住故。然於境界起戲論愛，隨所當生，即彼形類中有而生。又中有眼猶如天眼，無有障礙，唯至生處。所趣無礙，如得神通，亦唯至生處。
items.en: At that time, the former self-love [for the previous body] no longer becomes active, since consciousness has already moved on. Yet towards the objects [of its next existence] it gives rise to a craving born of elaboration, and takes on the form appropriate to whatever it is about to be born as. The intermediate being's sight, moreover, is like divine sight, unobstructed, though reaching only as far as its destined place of birth; and its movement, too, is unobstructed, as though it possessed supernormal power — yet again, only as far as that same destined place.

items.title: The Intermediate Being's Sight, Lifespan, and Destination

items.zh: 又由此眼，見己同類中有有情、及見自身當所生處。又造惡業者，眼視下淨，伏面而行；往天趣者上；往人趣者傍。
items.en: Further, by this sight, one sees other intermediate beings of one's own kind, and sees the very place one is about to be born. Further, one who has done unwholesome deeds looks downwards, taking what is below to be pleasant, and moves with face turned down; one bound for the heavens looks upwards; one bound for the human realm looks to the side.

items.zh: 又此中有，若未得生緣，極七日住。有得生緣，即不決定。若極七日未得生緣，死而復生，極七日住。如是展轉未得生緣，乃至七七日住，自此已後，決得生緣。
items.en: Further, this intermediate being, if it has not yet met the conditions for birth, lasts at most seven days. If it has met those conditions, its duration is not fixed. If, after a full seven days, it still has not met the conditions for birth, it dies and is at once reborn as another intermediate being, again lasting at most seven days. In this way, turning over again and again without meeting the conditions for birth, it may last up to seven times seven days — but beyond that, it will certainly meet the conditions for birth.

items.zh: 又此中有，七日死已，或即於此類生。若由餘業可轉中有種子轉者，便於餘類中生。
items.en: Further, when this intermediate being dies after its seven days, it may then be born as the very same kind [it currently appears as]. Or, if some other karma is able to alter the intermediate being's seed, it is instead born as a different kind altogether.

blocks.text: Yesterday ended with the state of mind at death. Today the treatise describes what the dying person perceives, the force that carries a being on to the next life, the physical signs of dying, and then the **intermediate being** (中有, *antarābhava*), the subtle body between one life and the next. It reads almost like a field guide, and our teachers treat it as practical instruction for caring for the dying and for preparing for our own death.

One passage, 0281c19–c23, is missing from Ru-Yi's translation, and we have supplied our own. It describes the frightening signs that come to someone who has done grave evil, and adds that for middling evil these signs may or may not appear, and not all of them.

subs.head: Two causes, and the foretokens of the next life

blocks.text: If good and bad habits are roughly equal, whatever comes to mind first is held to alone. Death then comes about through two dominant causes: **delight in elaboration** (戲論, the grasping we met on Day 1) and pure or impure karma.

As the karma of this life is used up, the karma of the next begins to show itself "as if in a dream". For someone going from light into darkness, the Buddha's simile is the late-afternoon sun as mountain shadows cover the land, first "partly", then "wholly", then "utterly". Venerable Miào Jìng explains 懸覆 ("partly overshadowed") as the shadow reaching over from far off, so the dying person first senses that the world is no longer bright. For someone going from darkness into light, the order is reversed, with agreeable forms appearing as in a dream.

This short passage is central to the whole account of rebirth. Right up until thought grows dim, the long-habituated **self-love** (我愛, *ātma-sneha*) becomes active: "I am about to cease to be," and one loves oneself all the more. "Through this, the intermediate state and the resulting rebirth are established."

Venerable Miào Jìng draws a technical distinction. Afflictions during life *initiate* karma (發業). Self-love at death *moistens* rebirth (潤生): like water on a seed already planted, it lets existing karma bear fruit. The seeds are already in the ālayavijñāna; craving at death is what makes them sprout.

Stream-enterers and once-returners still feel self-love at death, but by the power of wisdom they examine it again and again and keep it in check, "as a strong man wrestling a weak one". For a non-returner, self-love no longer arises at all. Venerable Miào Jìng adds that a non-returner is still reborn, in the Pure Abodes, through the remaining *seeds* of affliction, even though no self-love becomes active.

"Loosening of the limbs" (解支節), the dissolution felt at death, occurs in every realm except among the gods and in the hells, and is severe for wrongdoers and mild for the virtuous. Consciousness then withdraws from the body gradually: from the top downwards for one who has done evil, from the feet upwards for one who has done good, but in both cases it leaves last from the region of the heart. Venerable Miào Jìng notes that the popular Chinese verse ("crown: a saint; eyes: a god; heart: a human; belly: a hungry ghost; knees: an animal; soles: hell") "is not what the *Yogācārabhūmi* says". The treatise's point is simpler: whatever the direction, the heart is where consciousness leaves last, and on Day 6 we will see that it is also where consciousness first takes hold.

Birth begins with the intermediate being, produced by the same two causes as death: the perfuming of elaboration and the perfuming of karma, made active by uninterrupted self-love. Death and birth are simultaneous, "like the two ends of a scale: as one end sinks, the other rises". Master Cháng Bǎi: death only seems to come first; in fact there is no gap.

The intermediate being has all its faculties complete. For a wrongdoer it looks like the dim light of a black sheep or a dark night; for the virtuous, like white cloth or a clear moonlit night. Venerable Miào Jìng is emphatic: "the intermediate being is not a ghost". Every realm of rebirth has one; even going to Amitābha's Pure Land, he says, involves an intermediate being until one is born in the lotus.

The intermediate being sees others of its kind and the place where it will be born. Those bound for lower realms look downwards; those bound for the heavens, upwards. If it does not meet the conditions for birth, it lasts at most seven days, then dies and arises again as an intermediate being, up to seven times seven days, after which it will certainly find the conditions. If it meets the conditions, its duration "is not fixed", and may be very short.

Two practical consequences follow. Master Cháng Bǎi sees here the scriptural basis for the East Asian custom of weekly memorial rites for forty-nine days. Venerable Miào Jìng advises doing them early, even on seven consecutive days, because the being may be reborn quickly. And since "other karma is able to alter the intermediate being's seed", this treatise, unlike the *Mahāvibhāṣā*, holds that the outcome is not yet fixed, which is why merit dedicated during this period can help.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, through the dominant force of which two causes does death come about?
options: self-love and ignorance
attention and contact
the cause of delight in elaboration and the cause of pure and impure karma
the parents' fluids and the ālayavijñāna
quiz.why: The text states plainly that death comes "through the dominant force of two causes: the dominant force of delight in elaboration, and the dominant force of pure and impure karma." Option A is the trap: self-love does enter the account, but only in §34, as an additional activating force, not as one of these two causes. B names two of the universal mental factors, which have nothing to do with the causes of death. D lists the conditions for conception in §42, not for dying.

quiz.q: The treatise says, "Through this, the intermediate state and the resulting rebirth are established." What does "this" refer to?
options: the parents' craving
the long-habituated self-love becoming active at death — "thinking 'I am about to cease to be,' one comes to love one's own self all the more"
the most purified divine sight
the instruction of a good teacher
quiz.why: The text says that as beings approach death, before thought grows dim, long-habituated self-love becomes active — "thinking 'I am about to cease to be,' one comes to love one's own self all the more. Through this, the intermediate state and the resulting rebirth are established." Venerable Miào Jìng points out that this is exactly the answer to the exam question "How is the intermediate being established?" He also distinguishes the afflictions that *initiate* karma during one's life from this deathbed self-love, which *moistens* rebirth (潤生) — helping karma that already exists to bear its fruit. Option A belongs to the account of conception in §41, not to the establishing of the intermediate being.

quiz.q: Which of the following correctly describes self-love at death among the noble ones?
options: for a non-returner, self-love no longer becomes active at that time at all
for a stream-enterer, self-love does not become active at all
for a once-returner, self-love becomes active and turns into attachment
all noble ones cling to self-love at death just as ordinary beings do
quiz.why: The text draws two tiers. For stream-enterers and once-returners, self-love "likewise becomes active," but through the power of wisdom they examine it "again and again, restraining it so as not to become attached," like a strong man wrestling a weak one. For a non-returner, "self-love no longer becomes active at that time at all." Option B collapses the two tiers; option C misses the point that the first two fruits restrain self-love rather than becoming attached. Venerable Miào Jìng adds that although a non-returner's self-love is no longer active, such a being has not yet entered nirvāṇa without remainder and still takes rebirth through the *seeds* of affliction.

quiz.q: What simile does the treatise use to show that death and birth are simultaneous?
options: like a lamp and its light
like a seed and its sprout
like dreaming and waking
like the two ends of a scale: as one end sinks, the other rises, at one and the same time
quiz.why: The text: "Death and birth are simultaneous, like the two ends of a scale: as one end sinks, the other rises, at one and the same time." Venerable Miào Jìng stresses that the rising and the sinking happen together. Option B, seed and sprout, implies a before and after — the very thing this simile rules out. A and C are not used here. Master Cháng Bǎi likewise reads the line as a deliberate correction: death only *looks* as if it comes first; in fact there is no interval between the two.

quiz.q: According to Venerable Miào Jìng, which of the following is correct about the intermediate being?
options: the intermediate being is a ghost
only beings headed for the three unhappy realms have an intermediate being
one reborn in the Pure Land of Sukhāvatī passes through no intermediate being
the intermediate being is not a ghost; it belongs to all realms — hell, ghosts, animals, humans, and gods — as the body one has before formally receiving the next result
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Let us not misunderstand — the intermediate being is not a ghost. … It belongs to hell, ghosts, animals, humans, and gods alike; before formally receiving the result, there is first the body of the intermediate being." The treatise itself describes the intermediate being of one who did wholesome deeds as "like the light off white cloth," so B is wrong. C is a common misconception: in the question-and-answer sessions he explains that going from here to Amitābha's land covers a distance in both space and time, "so there must also be an intermediate being"; only after birth in the lotus is it no longer one.

quiz.q: Which of the following correctly states how long, according to the treatise, an intermediate being lasts?
options: if it has not met the conditions for birth, it lasts at most seven days; if not, it dies and is reborn as another intermediate being, up to seven times seven days, after which it will certainly meet the conditions for birth
every intermediate being lasts exactly forty-nine days
every intermediate being lasts exactly seven days
there is no limit; an intermediate being can remain indefinitely
quiz.why: "This intermediate being, if it has not yet met the conditions for birth, lasts at most seven days. If it has met those conditions, its duration is not fixed." If seven days pass without the conditions, it dies and is reborn as another intermediate being, "up to seven times seven days — but beyond that, it will certainly meet the conditions for birth." B and C both go wrong with "every" — once the conditions are met the duration is "not fixed" and may be very short. D contradicts "it will certainly meet the conditions." Master Cháng Bǎi takes the seven-times-seven-days as the scriptural basis for the East Asian weekly memorial rites.
